name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act
full_name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (Oregon Revised Statutes 646A.570 to 646A.589)
issuing_body: State of Oregon; published by the Oregon Legislature
notice: Assessed against ORS 646A.570 to 646A.589 as published in the Oregon Revised Statutes chapter 646A page of the Oregon Legislature.

control_flags.objectives: The lettered paragraphs of a subsection whose lead-in states the duty; each is required unless the lead-in makes them a choice.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable requirements that are implemented. The Act defines no score; this percentage is an HCG measure of progress.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.

The Act applies to a business that conducts business in Oregon or serves Oregon residents and, in a calendar year, controls or processes personal data of 100,000 or more consumers, or of 25,000 or more while earning over 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data.
A consumer request is answered without undue delay and within 45 days of receipt; the period may be extended once by 45 days.
rules.quote: not later than 45 days after receiving the request

rules.summary: Data protection assessments are kept for at least five years.
rules.quote: A controller shall retain for at least five years all data protection assessments

consequences.summary: The Attorney General can seek a civil penalty of up to $7,500 for each violation, or an injunction.
consequences.quote: civil penalty of not more than $7,500 for each violation

glossary.definition: The Oregon Consumer Privacy Act, Oregon's comprehensive consumer privacy law, in force since 1 July 2024.
The person that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
A person that processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

Personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, health diagnosis, sexual orientation, citizenship or immigration status; genetic or biometric data used to identify a person; data of a known child; and precise geolocation data.

A documented assessment, required before targeted advertising, sale of personal data, certain profiling and processing of sensitive data, that weighs the benefits of processing against the risks to consumers.
